@Video 1 · 5s controls the beach, bicycle motion, dialogue timing, lighting and color. Its audio plays continuously and unchanged: "Watch this. With just one photo, I can swap myself into whoever I want." @Video 2 · 2s is an ENDING REFERENCE only; finish on its LAST FRAME, matching the supplied end frame. @Image 1 is Adil's face identity.
ONE continuous 5-second cinema take. Adil is the ONLY person in the entire clip. There are no character swaps, no transformations, no other identities, no bald man, no jelly figure and no material changes. He stays the same man, in the same beige open shirt, white tee and light trousers, on the same bicycle, from the first frame to the last.
IDENTITY LOCK: Adil matches @Image 1 in every readable frame — oval face, warm olive skin, dark almond eyes, straight nose, thick dark chevron moustache, dense short black curls, small silver hoop earrings. His face stays stable and recognizable under the close wide-angle selfie perspective and remains identical after the camera pulls back. No identity drift, no face wobble, no age or feature shift between the close view and the wide view.
CAMERA: the first frame is already a close wide-angle selfie view with the camera gripped in Adil's RIGHT hand while his LEFT hand steers. Subtle realistic hand-held life: low-amplitude irregular tremor from grip tension, breathing, pedaling and uneven sand, tiny wrist rotations, delayed shoulder pulses and natural corrective settling — never digital jitter. He then performs a real physical release: fingers open one by one, the palm flattens, the camera lifts away with the residual velocity of his arm and tilts briefly before a stabilizer levels it, and his freed right hand travels down a visible physical path and closes on the handlebar grip. The hand never fades, stretches, thins away or vanishes. The camera then flies backward in one long smooth deceleration arc and returns exactly to @Video 1 · 5s's original frontal tracking angle, height, distance and centered composition. Level horizon, no roll, no whip pan, no framing jump. Continuous background parallax proves real forward travel — sand, puddles and horizon slide past without pause and the bicycle never pedals in place. Focal length, depth of field and background blur stay constant.
PERFORMANCE: Adil delivers the whole line himself with precise lip-sync to @Video 1 · 5s's audio — correct mouth shapes per consonant and vowel, visible teeth and tongue on plosives, natural lateral and rotational jaw motion, breath between words, never mechanical flapping. He adds a couple of confident playful head accents on the beats — a quick tilt or snap of the head to the side and back with the neck leading, shoulders following a beat later and his curls lagging and settling with real inertia — but his identity never changes; it is only body language. Living face: brow movement, orbicularis tension, cheek lifts, nostril flare on breath, asymmetric mouth corners, irregular blinking, saccadic gaze shifts, squinting into sun and wind, and expression that evolves through the line.
SKIN AND EYES: unretouched documentary realism — zone-varying pores, fine vellus hair in sunlight, oil sheen on nose, forehead and cheekbones, dry matte cheeks, uneven pigmentation, faint capillaries, moles, small blemishes, sun redness, subsurface scattering in ears, nostrils and lips, chapped lip texture, light sweat from riding. Eyes with wet corneas reflecting sky, sea and sand, iris fiber detail and daylight pupil size. No beauty filter, plastic sheen, pore-free cheeks, airbrushing, glowing complexion or dead doll stare.
LIGHT AND ENVIRONMENT: keep @Video 1 · 5s's exact sun — same direction, height, hardness, shadow length and softness, same sky fill, same warm bounce off bright sand under the jaw, nose and forearms — constant from the first frame to the last, with no flattening toward the end. Correct moving contact shadow under the bicycle and accurate reflections in wet sand and puddles. Match exposure, white balance, contrast curve, highlight rolloff, grade, lens distortion, grain, chromatic aberration and motion blur to the source. Sea wind moves his curls and open shirt in the source direction; the fabric has real weight, folds and flutter.
RIGID ANCHORS: the bicycle never changes — identical frame geometry and green paint, handlebar shape and grips, front basket, wheels, spokes, saddle and pedals from first to last frame, no bending, thickening, recoloring, wobbling or dissolving. Hands always physically wrap the grips with separated fingers, visible knuckles and contact pressure, correct five-finger anatomy; no hand melts into or passes through the handlebar and no fused fingers.
MANDATORY END LOCK: settle exactly onto the LAST FRAME of @Video 2 · 2s and the supplied end frame. BOTH hands on the handlebar, Adil centered, riding almost directly toward camera in a medium-wide full-body view, bicycle frontal, LEFT leg at the bottom of the pedal stroke and RIGHT leg bent at the top, head level, open beige shirt trailing in the wind. Match identity, pose, camera height, distance, cyclist scale, bicycle angle, horizon level, beach geometry, puddles, exposure, depth of field, light direction and color exactly. The last frames stay stable, level and clean with continuous forward travel and no reframing, drift, zoom or dive, so the clip cuts seamlessly in an editing timeline.
One unbroken take. No duplicate limbs, extra people, text, logos or added voices. Preserve wheel rotation, tire contact with sand and pedaling physics.

EDIT @Video 3 · 5s (8 seconds, one daylight beach location for the whole clip). Replace the rider with the deadpan yellow cow from @Image 5 for the ENTIRE video. The clip is one single continuous shot with one gorgeously smooth flow between its two phases — that flow is the star of the edit.
THE FLOW: the shot opens close on the cow's face in the handheld selfie view, alive and talking. His big hoofed hand sweeps across the lens exactly as in the source — same path, same speed, same timing — and the view pours seamlessly into the wide riding shot in one liquid, weightless motion: the framing melts open, the beach spreads, and he is already rolling toward us on the little green bicycle, still mid-sentence, while the camera glides backward in step with him. The whole passage between phases feels like silk — one breath, one current, butter-smooth, with the sweep of the hand, the widening of the frame, the flowing sand and the constant level horizon all belonging to one uninterrupted movement. The camera keeps living inertia after the reveal, easing gently as it settles into pace with the bike. Light, warmth and exposure flow continuously through the passage — one sun, one grade, one world on both sides, so the eye slides through without ever catching on anything.
CONTINUITY OF THE CHARACTER THROUGH THE FLOW: the same cow, the same fur, the same face, the same relaxed body groove carries straight through — his speech never pauses, his rhythm never resets, the pedal cadence he rolls in with feels like the natural continuation of the energy he had in the selfie. He occupies the source rider's exact screen space at every moment, and the bicycle, beach, puddles and horizon are the source's own, untouched.
LIVING EYES: his eyes are alive in every frame. Pupils hold the lens and counter-rotate against every bob of his head so the gaze stays locked on camera; quick small saccades between words; one slow bored half-blink mid-line with soft lid tension and skin drag around the orbit; moist corneas carrying a moving glint of the bright sky; daylight pupils. In the wide phase the eyes keep glinting, blinking and re-aiming at the lens as the bike bobs. Sleepy attitude means slow-moving eyes, never motionless ones.
PLATE-PERFECT INTEGRATION: the cow inherits the plate's photography completely. His sharpness never exceeds the background's; the plate's film grain, sensor noise and motion blur sit ON his fur and nose in every frame. He is lit only by the scene: hard warm sun from behind-right with a strong golden rim along his shoulder, ears, horns and fur edge; clear lit and shadow sides across the muzzle; warm sand bounce from below; cool sky tone on top. A firm dark contact shadow with ambient occlusion rides under both tires, the pedals and his body at all times, matching the sun; his hooves shade the pedals. The mirror-wet sand and every puddle he passes carry his yellow reflection and the green bike with correct perspective and blur; the chrome handlebar and rims flash with sky glints; sea haze and drifting sand float between him and the lens. He reads as a practical creature filmed on location — no cutout edge, no halo, nothing cleaner than the plate, especially along the fur silhouette against the sky.
THE COW: exactly @Image 5's stylized design — tall anthropomorphic cow in dense mustard-yellow fur with a pale cream chest, huge glossy pink nose with bumpy pores and oval nostrils, heavy half-closed sleepy eyelids over amber eyes, two small dark curved horns, floppy ears, braided fur band across the brow. Not a real cow. Fur flows in the sea wind as one continuous silky surface, never flickering.
PERFORMANCE: deadpan and unimpressed, exact source dialogue timing and audio unchanged. Close phase: "Watch this. With just one photo, I can swap myself into whoever I want. Or…" — soft muzzle lips shaping each phoneme, teeth glimpsed on plosives, pink nose flexing subtly, ears twitching lazily. Wide phase: "…teleport to a completely new location" with a fully animated mouth and a slow unimpressed glance into the lens — the same beach rolling on, which is the joke. Riding groove: hooves locked to the pedals in smooth continuous circles, wheels rolling in exact step with the ground, tires pressing glistening tracks, ears and jowls with soft secondary motion over the bumps — everything cycles, nothing hesitates.
The bicycle keeps its exact source design — green frame, handlebar, basket, wheels, saddle, pedals — hoofed fingers wrapped on the grips with visible pressure. One location, one take, one continuous flow. No extra people, no text, no logos.

CAMERA = INPUT CAMERA, FRAME-FOR-FRAME, ALL 23 SECONDS — THIS OVERRIDES EVERYTHING BELOW. COPY ITS MOTION EVEN IF EVERYTHING ELSE FAILS.
V2V on @Video 11 · 23s — TRANSFORMATION OVERLAY, NOT a regeneration. Keep the real man, his bike, his riding, the beach geography and the CAMERA 1:1; duration matches source (~23s). We ADD, strictly ONE THING AT A TIME: a jump-cut to the purple dusk of @Image 7 (~1s) → a WHEELIE (4–10s) → the dog of @Image 8 in at 5s, scared off at 11s → two galleons breaching (11–15s) → the colossal kraken (15–19s) → tribal hunters entering mid-ground left in growing waves (14–21s) → jump-cut back (21s–end).
═ ACTIVE REFERENCES ═
@Image 1 — ADIL'S FACE ONLY: identity lock for his face every frame, every angle, no drift. Take NOTHING else from it — wardrobe and bike stay per @Video 11 · 23s (cream linen suit over white tee, pale bike with basket).
@Image 7 — WEATHER / GRADE ASSET: after the ~1s jump-cut the world becomes EXACTLY this dusk — deep violet sky grading through purple into a soft rose band at the horizon, thin dark cloud streaks, first stars, the calm sea in layered purple wave-lines, dark wet mirror sand carrying the sky's reflection, deep soft foreground shadow. Match palette, exposure, contrast and mood 1:1, hold until 21s. He is RE-LIT into it: purple ambient on the suit, soft rose rim, wet reflection under the tires.
@Image 8 — THE DOG (design lock): this exact rough-coated JACK RUSSELL TERRIER — compact white body, tan-brown patches on the head and ears and at the tail base, white blaze down the forehead, wiry scruffy coat, bearded muzzle, dark round eyes, stubby upright tail. Appearance only — in the scene he is graded INTO the dusk (purple ambient on the white coat, never bright-white against the plate, wet reflections, contact shadows).
═ RULE #0 · CAMERA — QUADRUPLE LOCK (highest; every conflict resolves in its favor) ═
LOCK 1 — COPY: output camera = input camera, 100% frame-for-frame, all 23s: position, framing, focal length, every drift, acceleration, deceleration, timing — INCLUDING the input's natural micro-imperfections: its tiny drift noise and organic sway are part of the motion, never smoothed, never stabilized, never idealized.
LOCK 2 — DESCRIBED: one continuous drone flight — 【0–2s】 backward retreat in front of the rider; 【2–6s】 ARC-OUT to his side, pulling back and rising, frontal → profile; 【6–16.5s】 frozen LATERAL PARALLEL TRACK at his speed, distance and height locked, world scrolling out the left edge; 【16.5–23s】 smooth DECELERATION to near-static as the white cabin enters frame-right.
LOCK 3 — CHECKPOINTS (mismatch = failure): t=0 frontal, rider ≈55% height; t=2 frontal ≈35%; t=4 three-quarter ≈18%; t=6 SIDE PROFILE ≈12%, horizon top third; t=8/10/12/14/16 identical — profile ≈10%, pinned x≈30%, background scrolling left at constant rate; t=16.5 cabin enters right edge; t=18 cabin ≈x60%; t=21 near-static, cabin ≈x65%; t=23 static, rider beside the cabin, ≈10% height.
LOCK 4 — FORBIDDEN: no push-in, pull-back, zoom, pan, tilt, reframe, shake, stabilization, smoothing or speed change for ANY added element — not for the dog's entry, not for the ships' breach, not for the kraken, not for the hunters; jump-cuts switch content only — the camera continues mid-phase through them; rider's scale never grows after 6.0s (re-growth = failure); horizon level every frame. The camera does not know the added elements exist. CAMERA = INPUT, START TO END.
═ RULE #1 · MOTION QUALITY LAW — NO SLOP MOVEMENT, EVER ═
WEIGHT: every body, paw, hull and tentacle accelerates and decelerates through real mass — nothing starts or stops instantly, nothing glides at constant speed. GROUND TRUTH: every step and paw-fall makes real contact — heel-strike, weight transfer, sand deformation, kicked clods, wet splashes; nothing slides, floats or moonwalks. NO LOOPS: no repeated gait cycles, no metronome rhythms, no mirrored or synced motion between any two beings; speeds fluctuate, paths wander and self-correct. ALIVE: heads scan, faces change through the take, chests breathe, cloth and hair answer the body a half-beat late, small mistakes get corrected in ugly human ways. WATER: splashes fall under gravity and drain, foam persists and drifts. One second of robotic, looped, floaty or synced movement anywhere = total failure.
═ RULE #2 · COLOR & LIGHT MATCH — EVERY ADDED PIXEL ═
Everything added is graded INTO the @Image 7 dusk: purple-violet ambient base; warm light ONLY from visible practicals (deck fires, torches, muzzle flashes) reaching only as far as real light would; rose rims from the horizon band; true contact shadows; wet-sand reflections under every paw, foot and hull; correct haze and focus falloff per depth; matched grain and exposure. Nothing brighter, sharper, cleaner or differently white-balanced than the plate. One mismatched element = pasted = failure.
═ ONE CONTINUOUS RIDE ═ The ride is continuous; the ONLY cuts are the world jump-cuts (~1s, ~14s, ~21s) — single-frame switches, him mid-pedal in the same screen position. The dog and hunters enter PHYSICALLY through frame edges, never by cut, never spawning mid-frame. No other cuts, no dissolves, no morphs.
═ SOURCE LOCK (the man) ═ Same man 1:1 — face per @Image 1, wardrobe and bike per @Video 11 · 23s. Riding path, speed and body motion per source EXCEPT the trick window (4–10s), then seamless re-sync. He stays COOL: at most one lazy glance over the shoulder. Identity drift or panic = failure.
═ STAGING MAP (hard positions) ═
- THE DOG enters and exits ONLY through the BOTTOM-LEFT frame edge (near-foreground sand).
- THE HUNTERS enter ONLY through the LEFT frame edge in the MID-GROUND — along the sandbar and shallow tide channel behind his riding line, at his depth or slightly deeper toward the water.
- The near-foreground sand (bottom-left) is used ONLY by the dog — no hunter ever enters or crosses the foreground; after the dog flees it stays EMPTY to the end.
- Ships and kraken live offshore only; splashes reach the sand, bodies never do.
═ TIMELINE (one thing at a time) ═
【~1s · JUMP-CUT TELEPORT】 ONE HARD CUT into the @Image 7 world: violet-to-rose dusk, first stars, layered purple wave-lines, wet mirror sand, deep soft foreground shadow. Same screen position, same pace, re-lit per the reference. Clean blink, no transition FX. Grade holds until 21s.
【4–10 · THE WHEELIE】 He compresses, pulls the FRONT WHEEL UP into a clean sustained WHEELIE — riding the rear wheel, arms taut, jacket flapping, visible wrist-level balance corrections, rear tire carving one line in the wet sand — holds ~4 seconds, drops the front wheel with a soft compression, rolls seamlessly back into the source line. No spins, no flourishes. Real weight per RULE #1. The camera does NOT adjust.
【5–11 · THE DOG — IN ON THE WHEELIE, SCARED OFF BY THE SHIPS】 At ~5.0s, just as the front wheel lifts, the @Image 8 Jack Russell bursts INTO frame through the BOTTOM-LEFT edge — asymmetric bouncy terrier gallop, head bobbing out of phase, tongue flapping, ears flying independently — catches up beside the bike and BARKS at him nonstop: irregular rhythm (two sharp, a skipped beat, a grumble, a volley), head throwing up on the big ones, beard bouncing, little wet-sand splashes off his paws, path wandering — surging, drifting wide, cutting back, one sideways skip-hop. At ~11.0s, on the FIRST surge-roar of the breaching ships, he SPOOKS: ears flatten, tail tucks, a scrambling panicked turn with kicked sand — and he bolts OUT through the bottom-left edge, gone for good. Never touches the bike, never crosses the front wheel. Conveyor-belt dog = failure.
【11–15 · THE SHIPS — BUOYANT BOUNCE】 Two huge pirate galleons (different silhouettes, one nearer one farther, ragged sails) BREACH offshore like released buoys: sea bulges → hull SURGES past its waterline — hangs — SINKS BACK past equilibrium — BOBS twice, diminishing, settles into a gentle pitch. Water avalanches off the decks each bob, rigging snaps taut, masts sway with inertia, displacement rings reach the shore as taller wave sets. Settled, they exchange ONE broadside each — real flashes, rolling smoke, geysers — then hold, small deck fires guttering in the wind. Fires and flashes their only warm light. Buoyancy, never rubber; never fade-in, never on the horizon. The camera does NOT look at them.
【15–19 · THE KRAKEN — COLOSSAL, AFTER THE SHIPS】 Only once both ships settle: the sea between them RISES in a hill-sized bulge and TENTACLES ONLY (body never shown) climb out — each THICKER THAN THE GALLEON'S HULL, rising TWO-THREE mast-heights, suckers the size of ship's boats, waterfalls pouring off, shadow across the whole nearer ship; wet skin picking up only purple sky and fire glints. Slow BECAUSE of the size — sagging, deforming where they grip — they wrap the nearer galleon like a hand around a toy and drag it down in one continuous heave: deck tilting, fires sliding, foam wall; the far ship holds fire and lists in the swell. Whirlpool wide as both ships; waves reach the sand. The galleon reads SMALL in the grip. Fast/thin tentacles or weightless ship = failure. The camera does NOT tilt.
【14–21 · THE HUNT — MID-GROUND LEFT, GROWING WAVES, REAL PEOPLE】 On one hard cut-beat at ~14s: THREE-FOUR tribal hunters burst INTO frame through the LEFT edge in the MID-GROUND — running in along the sandbar and tide channel behind his line — locked on HIM: pointing at him, spears leveled toward the bike, a barked order sending two to flank. The pack GROWS in waves: 3–4 more at ~16s, another 6–8 at ~18s, a horde of 20–25 by ~20s — all entering left mid-ground, never the foreground, never spawning mid-frame; thin front → deep tail stretching back along the sandbar. Woven grass-and-cloth attire, carved spears, torches (their only warm light; purple ambient on skin and cloth; individual shadows; wet reflections underfoot). ALIVE per RULE #1: speeds fluctuating, paths wandering around the tide pools, heads turning to shout and glance at the kraken, faces changing through the take, chests heaving, one stumble on soft sand recovered in two ugly human steps, gestures relayed down the line. ONE comedy beat: one hunter face-plants into a tide pool, somersaults, pops up running while the nearest one cackles. They gain along the sandbar, never reach him, never touch him, true mid-ground scale always — never enlarged, never foreground. The camera does NOT reframe.
【21s–end · THE RETURN】 ONE HARD CUT back: pastel daylight, empty calm beach — nothing added remains, no residue — the source plate continuing untouched to the white cabin. Last ~2s pure original footage.
═ CLEAR PATH ═ Nothing ever crosses his front wheel; no added element ever overlaps his body; the near-foreground stays empty except the dog's entry and exit.
═ RULES ═ CAMERA per the quadruple lock, micro-imperfections copied, checkpoints hit, zero reaction to every event (outranks all); face per @Image 1 only; weather/grade per @Image 7 1–21s; dog per @Image 8, in at 5s bottom-left, barking beside him, spooked at 11s by the ships' first roar, out bottom-left, never returns; hunters ONLY left mid-ground along the sandbar, waves 3–4 → 20–25, hunting HIM; MOTION QUALITY LAW on everything (one second robotic/looped/floaty/synced = failure); max TWO added systems in motion at once (dog exits at 11 as the ships rise; far ship passive when the kraken rises); jump-cuts only at ~1s/~14s/~21s; voiceover 1:1; wheelie only, 4–10s; exactly 1 dog, 2 ships, 1 kraken (tentacles only), hunters per waves; color & light match on every added pixel; no gore, no logos, no readable text, no IP. Soft linen and cotton with natural folds and light creases, apron fabric draping with real weight, hair holding natural curl with slight movement, jewelry sitting with weight. The remote (prop)
SCENE CONTEXT A single modern 4K Smart TV remote control prop, stripped down to a minimal button set, presented as a clean three-view product reference: front face, true side profile, and back shell. No hands, no environment, object only on a flat neutral medium-grey seamless background. OBJECT Slim minimalist Smart TV remote, contemporary 2020s design language, matte-black soft-touch polymer body, rounded corners, thin tapered thickness. Reduced, primitive button layout — no streaming-app shortcut buttons (no Netflix, Prime Video, YouTube, Disney), no mic button, no back/home buttons. Front face layout, top to bottom: A single round power button at the very top-right. Directly below the power area, a "higgs 4K" wordmark in bright lime-chartreuse green, hex #D2F84E — sized slightly smaller than a hero logo, compact and tidy in the upper face, not oversized. Below the logo, a large central circular navigation ring with a glossy black round OK/select key in the middle and a thin chrome ring; four directional arrows (up, down, left, right) printed on the ring at top, bottom, left and right positions. Below the ring, two simple control pairs side by side: a volume rocker on the left (a "+" key above a "−" key, small "VOL" label) and a channel rocker on the right (an up-chevron above a down-chevron, small "CH" label). Clean, uncluttered, lots of empty matte-black space, premium minimalist aesthetic. Back shell: smooth tapered surface with a subtle recessed battery-compartment cover and a small "higgs 4K" logo in lime-chartreuse #D2F84E near the bottom. LAYOUT Three identical remotes arranged left to right on the same horizontal baseline, evenly spaced, equal scale. Left = front view, face toward camera, fully readable. Center = strict side profile, edge-on in plane, showing thickness and slightly raised buttons in silhouette. Right = back view, rear shell toward camera. Object centered vertically, generous equal margins, no overlap, no cropping. OPTICS 47° diagonal field of view, standard normal lens character, camera 3 to 4 meters back, zero distortion, straight rectilinear edges, natural proportions, deep depth of field so all three views stay razor-sharp front to back. CAMERA Eye-level, locked static, dead-on orthographic framing for each view. No perspective tilt, no foreshortening. LIGHTING Even soft studio softbox key from the front-upper, broad and shadowless, subtle gradient falloff on the grey background. Soft contact shadow directly beneath each remote to anchor it. No harsh reflections, no blown speculars, matte surfaces read as matte, the lime logo stays saturated and clean. MATERIAL Soft-touch polymer absorbs light, rubber buttons show faint sheen, the lime-chartreuse "higgs 4K" logo reads as crisp colored print, chrome navigation ring shows a thin clean highlight. Pristine, dust-free, no fingerprints. POSITIVE LOCKS Minimal primitive 4K Smart TV remote only — buttons limited to: power, central directional ring with OK and four arrows, volume rocker, channel rocker. No app shortcut buttons, no mic, no back/home keys. No hands, no props, no text overlays except the "higgs 4K" logo and the small VOL/CH labels and arrow glyphs. prompt:
Treat prop sheets the same way as character sheets: grey background, multiple views.
Here's a real lesson from this step: the GPT Image 2 results looked flat - no depth, no shadows, and Seedance might render that as a 2D object. We switched to Nano Banana Pro with the same prompt, and the remote got depth, highlights, and realistic tapered edges. There's no single best model for everything - if the result isn't what you wanted, switch the model or tweak the prompt.
The first video
With all assets ready, we uploaded them to Claude and described the shot: the character walks into the room, sits on the couch, and turns on the TV - one continuous handheld take with optical flares.
SCENE CONTEXT Evening. @ADIL comes home, crosses his living room, sits on the sofa facing the TV, picks up the remote and switches it on — one unbroken take. From the unseen kitchen his mother calls in English that food is almost ready; he answers without taking his eyes off the screen.ACTIVE REFERENCES @ADIL — young man, tired end-of-day, settling into his own space. 100% matches the reference. @REMOTE — ordinary household TV remote. 100% matches the reference. (Mother is an offscreen English voice only — no in-frame reference, never enters the shot.)LOCATION MAP @ADIL'S-ROOM — STYLE REFERENCE ONLY, not a fixed keyframe; model extends the world, the subject moves through real space, never pinned 1:1. Foreground: doorway / hallway frame-right leading off to an unseen kitchen. Midground: the sofa, facing forward. Background: the far wall with the flatscreen TV. A side window sits frame-left as the light source. Lived-in room, soft daylight, dust and faint haze in the air.FIRST FRAME / BLOCKING Non-empty opening frame: @ADIL caught mid-step in the doorway, three-quarter back to camera, hand brushing the frame, the room opening up ahead of him with the TV visible on the far wall directly forward. Sofa in the midground between him and the TV. Asymmetric framing, subject already in motion.FORMAT MODE One continuous shot — the camera does not cut on its own. No edits, no transitions.OPTICS Continuous evolving reframe inside the single take: opens MS at 47° from three-quarter behind, arcs around to the front and eases to a waist-level MS on the remote, then settles into an MCU at 29° on hands and face as the TV ignites. Rectilinear with anamorphic optical flares, prime-lens character, 180° shutter motion blur.CAMERA One continuous handheld take, live operator breathing, organic shake and micro-drift, a subtle dutch that resettles. Eye-level following him in from three-quarter behind as window flares streak past, arcing to the front as he sits, dropping to a slightly low waist-level reframe onto @REMOTE in his hand as he answers his mother, then drifting tighter onto hands and face for the click. Focus rides with him. Camera on the shadow side; operator axis travels from behind to front. The lens never stops moving — one unbroken move motivated by following him home and landing on the click.ACTION Subject: steps in through the doorway, eyes scanning, unhurried walk toward the sofa, shoulders dropping; sits down facing the TV with a settling exhale; tips his head slightly toward the hallway as his mother calls, answers back without looking away, hand reaching and closing around @REMOTE on the cushion; lifts @REMOTE, aims it forward at the TV, a half-beat pause, thumb presses — soft click — the screen ignites and cool glow washes back across his face from ahead. Camera: described in CAMERA — one continuous following move, behind to front to medium-close, no self-cuts.PERFORMANCE Tired end-of-day release: a slow exhale with visible chest rise as he sits, shoulders loosening, jaw unclenching. Eyes drift low, then catch the screen light — a small flicker of anticipation, lips parting slightly. Pore-level realism: vellus hair, capillary flush, wet living eyes with catch-lights from the screen.PHYSICS @REMOTE carries real weight in his hand. The cushion compresses and the fabric shifts as he sits. Correct contact shadows under him on the sofa and on the floor. Nothing floats.LIGHTING Natural light only. Soft window daylight key from frame-left, camera on the shadow side, atmospheric haze carrying the optical flares at roughly 10–15 meters depth. As the TV ignites, its cool screen glow becomes a second key from directly in front, washing his face from ahead. WB locked 5200K.COLOR GRADE Warm lived-in room neutrals as the dominant material, cool window light and TV glow as the secondary beam, and a chartreuse #d1ef17 accent living only in the TV standby LED, the first flicker of the screen, and a single glint catching a lens flare — color tied to source and surface, not a flat list.AUDIO NO MUSIC. SFX ONLY — diegetic sound and live audio throughout. No score, no soundtrack, no background music of any kind. Room ambience, footsteps on the floor, the soft compression of the cushion, a soft remote click, the low power-on hum of the TV. Dialogue (English, audio only, no subtitles): Mother (offscreen, from the kitchen): "Food's almost ready, sweetie!" @ADIL (answering, eyes on the screen): "Okay, Mom — coming soon!"STYLE 8K photorealistic — no 3D render, no game engine, no game-cutscene aesthetic. Naturalistic master cinematography, anamorphic optical flares, fine film grain.OUTPUT SETTINGS 16:9. Real-time throughout, no slow-motion.POSITIVE LOCKS One continuous shot, the camera does not cut on its own. The TV stays on the far wall directly in front of the sofa and in @ADIL's eyeline — he faces it, screen glow comes from ahead of him. @REMOTE stays normal household remote size. The mother stays offscreen, an English voice only. TV screen content stays abstract and unbranded — plain glow, no logos, no UI, no subtitles. Contact shadows on sofa and floor read clearly. Wardrobe comes from the @ADIL reference and stays identical across the whole take. Eyes stay natural — no eye glow.

scene: Scene 2 - The fantasy flight on the TV
prompt:
For characters from scratch, Soul Cinema is the best and the cheapest - 1 credit for 8 images
SCENE CONTEXT @woman flies on @fantasy-dragon, a large flying creature, through a colossal jungle of mile-high fantastical trees. Wordless throughout, she steers with her body and pure joy — laughing and whooping as @fantasy-dragon pulls off daring tricks: a sheer near-vertical plunge down an immensely tall 90° waterfall almost grazing the water, a low skim across the pool, passing through a cloud of giant butterflies with a single breathtaking slow-motion moment, gliding between branches and lianas past leaping monkeys, threading a razor-narrow gap, then climbing straight up the trunks and bursting above the canopy into a vast reveal of the whole world. One continuous soaring flight.ACTIVE REFERENCES @fantasy-dragon: the flying creature. 100% matches the reference, identical design every frame. @woman: the rider, seated just behind @fantasy-dragon's shoulders, hands on its shoulder-ridge, leaning, ducking and bracing into every bank, dive and roll. 100% matches the reference, same person throughout.CREATURE SCALE & WING PHYSICS (behavior only, design from reference) @fantasy-dragon is large — wingspan of a small aircraft, body big enough to carry @woman easily, powerful and substantial. Its wings obey real flight physics with three clear modes: (1) in the vertical dive, wings tuck in tight and folded against the body, streamlined for a fast nose-down plunge; (2) when gliding and weaving through the trees, wings hold wide, spread and still, soaring on locked wings — steering by tilting and angling the spread wings and body, not by flapping; (3) when climbing and gaining height, broad, deliberate, weighty wingbeats with a clear up- and down-stroke through a large arc, the membrane flexing and the whole body rising and dipping with each beat. Mass and inertia read in every motion.FORMAT MODE Single continuous take with no cuts. One in-camera speed ramp: real-time motion throughout, ramping down smoothly into super slow motion for a single butterfly close-up around the 4–6s mark, then snapping back hard and instantly to full real-time speed. Real-time everywhere else. 15 seconds, 16:9 anamorphic widescreen. The clip is purely visual and sound-effect driven, with a fully music-free, speech-free, caption-free track — natural ambience and the rider's wordless voice only.CAMERA POSITION LOCK — ALWAYS BEHIND The camera stays locked behind @fantasy-dragon and @woman for the entire clip — a chase camera that follows directly from the rear, holding their backs in frame with the world rushing toward and past them. We always see them from behind: the back of @woman's head and shoulders, @fantasy-dragon's wings filling the foreground, the jungle opening up ahead. During the slow-motion beat the camera keeps its rear position and simply racks focus onto a butterfly hovering close to the lens, with @fantasy-dragon and @woman gliding softly just beyond it. The camera rides their tail through the dive, skim, glide, gap and climb, keeping the same rear vantage throughout.THE LOCATION (full description — maximum color and life) A surreal, monumental rainforest of impossible scale. The trees are mile-high fantastical giants — colossal pillar-trunks wider than towers, bark in deep browns and mossy greens, crowns vanishing into golden mist; upper branches fuse into vaulted green cathedral arches. Thick horizontal branches and long hanging lianas cross the flight path at many depths, and one pair of trunks leans together to form a razor-narrow vertical gap. A colossal, immensely tall waterfall drops in a sheer, near-vertical 90° wall — a vast curtain of falling water plunging straight down an enormous cliff-trunk from high in the canopy, falling and falling all the way to the forest floor, into a glowing turquoise pool and mist-filled gorge, sunlight throwing rainbows across the spray. The whole jungle blazes with color and life: cascading flowers in magenta, violet, orange and gold, glowing bioluminescent blooms, hanging curtains of pink and blue blossom, giant lily-pads and lotus on the pool, emerald spiral ferns, turquoise moss, dangling vines heavy with fruit, oversized jewel-toned leaves, drifting seed-pods and floating spores catching the light. It teems with diverse wildlife at every depth — dense flocks of brilliant birds (scarlet macaw-like fliers, cobalt songbirds, gold-and-green parrots, iridescent hummingbirds, big slow herons over the water), vast drifting swarms of giant luminous butterflies in sapphire, amber and emerald, dragonflies and glowing fireflies, troops of long-limbed monkeys swinging and leaping from tree to tree, neon tree-frogs and chameleons on the trunks, a coiled serpent on a branch, a pair of huge gentle deer-like grazers and a family of small spotted creatures drinking at the pool far below. High screen-right, warm golden sun rakes down through the canopy in thick volumetric god-rays, catching waterfall-mist, pollen and floating spores. Everything alive is tiny against the trees. Deep parallax: foreground vines, flowers and leaves rush past, midground trunks and wildlife slide by, the far canopy and sky shift slowly behind.FIRST FRAME AND SPATIAL BLOCKING The first visible frame already contains @fantasy-dragon and @woman, seen from behind, hanging high at the very top of the immensely tall 90° waterfall — tiny against the towering wall of water, already tipping nose-down into the vertical plunge with wings folding in. The camera sits directly behind them. @fantasy-dragon center frame, x 50%, y 40%, wings tucking tight, pointing straight down the falling water; @woman just ahead of the lens on its back, leaning low and forward into the dive, the back of her head and streaming hair in frame, laughing. The flight path drops straight down the huge waterfall almost touching its surface, flares open just above the pool, skims the water, rises into the butterflies and the slow-motion beat, glides through the trees, threads the narrow gap, then climbs upward — always viewed from the rear.OPTICS 107° diagonal field of view, wide rectilinear lens character, camera held very close — 0.5–0.8 m behind @fantasy-dragon's back and wings, almost riding with them. Immediate foreground (@fantasy-dragon's wings and body, @woman's streaming hair, rushing spray, vines and butterflies) looms large; the surrounding jungle spreads wide to all frame edges; straight trunk lines stay straight and rectilinear edge to edge, with subtle chromatic aberration near the corners. During the super-slow-motion beat, the same wide lens racks focus to a single giant butterfly hovering right at the lens, rendering it in crisp, detailed close-up while @fantasy-dragon and @woman soften slightly just beyond — no lens cut, a smooth focus pull. Immersive, body-near, action-cam-mounted-behind-the-rider intimacy with huge environmental width.ACTION TIMING 0.0s–3.0s — THE TALL PLUNGE & WATER SKIM: from directly behind, @fantasy-dragon tips over the very top of the immensely tall 90° waterfall and drops in a long near-vertical nose-down plunge, wings tucked tight and folded, streamlined and accelerating straight down the towering wall of falling water — flying down so close it almost grazes the rushing surface the whole way, spray and rainbow light streaking past. Near the forest floor it flares its wings wide open and arcs out of the dive, leveling inches above the glowing turquoise pool, wingtips and tail-fan slicing twin lines of spray, herons scattering ahead. @woman trails her fingers through the water, shrieking with joy. 3.0s–4.0s — INTO THE SWARM: @fantasy-dragon rises off the water with a few powerful wingbeats toward a vast cloud of giant luminous butterflies; as they approach, the swarm bursts apart and scatters in every direction — sapphire, amber and emerald wings whirling outward around them. @woman laughs, arms wide. 4.0s–6.0s — SUPER SLOW-MOTION BUTTERFLY (no cut): as they pass through the swarm, one large butterfly drifts up right to the lens and time ramps smoothly down into super slow motion, holding for about two seconds on a beautiful close-up of this single butterfly — its big iridescent wings beating slowly and gracefully, every detail visible: glowing sapphire-amber-emerald scales, fine vein patterns, light shining through the translucent membrane, tiny shimmering edges — while @fantasy-dragon and @woman glide on softly just behind it. Then, sharply and instantly, time snaps back to full real-time speed — a hard, sudden return to motion as the butterfly whips away and the flight surges forward again. 6.0s–9.0s — THE GLIDING WEAVE PAST THE MONKEYS: back at full speed, @fantasy-dragon spreads its wings wide and still and soars on locked wings, gliding silently between two massive crossing branches and a curtain of hanging lianas, banking and tilting on its spread wings — no flapping — leaves, fruit and flowers whipping past. Troops of long-limbed monkeys leap from tree to tree across the path and cling to the trunks, heads snapping round to stare after @fantasy-dragon and @woman in wide-eyed surprise as they glide by; parrots and hummingbirds scatter. @woman ducks low and lets out a delighted whoop. 9.0s–11.5s — THE NARROW GAP: still gliding, @fantasy-dragon folds its wings and shoots through a razor-narrow vertical gap between two leaning trunks — bark walls blurring past inches from the lens — then snaps its wings open on the far side in a corkscrew roll past a swooping flock. @woman throws her head back, laughing and cheering with pure exhilaration. 11.5s–15.0s — THE CLIMB AND REVEAL: @fantasy-dragon pitches up and powers straight upward along the colossal trunks with broad, heaving wingbeats, bark, branches, flowers and birds streaking downward past the lens as the camera (still behind) tilts up and cranes back. They burst up through the top of the canopy into open golden sky. The camera pulls back into a colossal wide establishing shot revealing the WHOLE world at once — an endless sea of mile-high trees rolling to the horizon, rivers of mist and the distant waterfall gorge between them, flocks like drifting confetti, @fantasy-dragon and @woman a bright speck rising above it all. @woman laughs breathlessly in wonder as @fantasy-dragon levels off and glances back at her with a soft chirp. Hold on the awe.PHYSICS @fantasy-dragon moves with the three wing modes above — wings tucked and streamlined in the long vertical plunge, wide and locked while gliding through the trees, broad and heaving while climbing. The flare out of the dive shows real aerodynamic load as the open wings catch the air and bend the fall into a level arc. In the slow-motion beat the butterfly's wingbeat reads in exquisite slow detail — wings flexing, bending and rippling through the stroke, scales catching light, body bobbing gently. Mass and inertia carry through every bank, roll, glide and level-out. Down the waterfall and over the water, wingtips and tail cut real spray trails and leave a wake; mist beads in the air. @woman's body shifts, ducks and braces with every move, weight transferring; her hair and clothes stream and snap with airspeed, gusts and spray. Branches, lianas, fruit, flowers, leaves and butterfly wings bend, scatter and recoil as they pass. Birds, butterflies, monkeys and ground animals react with real evasive and curious motion — monkeys leaping between trees and turning to look. Every motion carries weight and momentum with clear acceleration and deceleration.LIGHTING Primary light is warm golden sun high on screen-right, raking through the canopy in volumetric god-rays and catching mist, pollen, spores and butterfly wings. Maximum vibrancy and luminosity — deep emerald and jade greens, cobalt-to-turquoise sky and pool, warm gold accents, blazing pops of scarlet, magenta, violet, sapphire and coral from flowers, butterflies, birds and @fantasy-dragon. During the slow-motion close-up, sunlight glows through the butterfly's translucent wings, lighting up the iridescent color. At the waterfall, sun through the spray throws a vivid rainbow and bright speculars off the water. Purely hand-drawn painterly 2D animation in every single frame: drawn lines, painted light, graphic silhouettes, fine film grain. Motion is drawn: smeared brush streaks for speed, snapping poses.
LIGHTING
Golden-hour sunset, clear dry evening, fully relit: a low blazing sun throwing long hard shadows, warm amber-gold key, orange bounce off the asphalt, deep teal-blue open shadows, the sky burning from gold through rose to deep violet. Sun flicker strobes through guardrail posts and lampposts in driving shots. The car's round headlights are dark until 2.0s, SWITCH ON during SHOT 3 with a warm bloom, and glow for the rest of the film. The cabin is lit by sunset through the glass and the warm glow of the old dashboard. Every light comes from a visible source; the whole film lives in this one dry sunset.
COLOR
Sunset palette: burning golds and ambers, rose and violet sky, long teal-blue shadows. Against it: the aged sea-teal car with cream roof and warm chrome, the grandpa's tweed and olive wool, the grandma's wine-red shawl as the sharpest accent — and in the finale the black-and-white police cars with pulsing red beacons. Thick white-grey tire smoke catches the sunset in the burnout shots.
CAMERA
All camera work comes from @Video 8 · 30s — 19 shots, its exact cut points, its exact moves; lens locked within each cut. STRONG anamorphic lens character: horizontal squeeze and compression, oval elliptical bokeh, horizontally stretched highlights, curved barrel edge distortion, chromatic aberration toward the edges. NO lens flares, NO light streaks, NO floating bokeh circles. Natural 180-degree shutter cadence: fast motion carries directional blur, hold points stay sharp, stable temporal cadence.
PHYSICS
For the first 4 seconds the car is STATIONARY, engine waking then building violence: the driven wheel spins in place, pouring thick tire smoke, the body squatting and trembling with torque. From the launch at ~4.05s the heavy old saloon reads FAST: the world stretches into directional streaks opposite to travel while the body stays relatively sharp; dust and smoke in the wake, heat shimmer, grit in the arches, soft suspension leaning, chrome trembling. Every wheel on screen turns with visible rotational motion blur whenever the car moves or the engine pulls. The grandma's shawl and yarn react to the drive.
RULES
1. VIDEO LOCK, ENDING LOCK and LOCATION CONTINUITY above govern everything.
2. SEATING, LHD: steering wheel on the LEFT. THE GRANDPA occupies the front-LEFT seat behind the wheel for all 30 seconds; THE GRANDMA occupies the front-RIGHT passenger seat for all 30 seconds; the rear bench carries the luggage. The car carries ALWAYS exactly two people, both present in every interior view and behind the glass in every exterior view. When the camera faces BACKWARD into the cabin, screen sides mirror: he reads frame-RIGHT, she frame-LEFT.
3. MOTION STATE: during 1.0-4.0s the car stands perfectly still, doing its burnout in place; from the launch at the start of SHOT 5 to the end it always drives FORWARD, nose-first, wheels rotating forward, exactly along the source trajectory.
4. DUMMY MAPPING: the front-LEFT sphere-head dummy (with its grey arm at the shifter and grey leg at the pedals) is THE GRANDPA; the front-RIGHT sphere-head dummy is THE GRANDMA; a front-seat dummy together with its loose blocks is that ONE whole person. Blocks on the rear bench are the luggage. The low-poly flying model in SHOT 18 is THE HELICOPTER. The two vehicles behind the hero car in SHOT 19 are THE POLICE CARS.
5. PRESENCE: a seated person stays drawn even when partially occluded — in every interior frame some part of each seat's owner is visible: a gloved hand, an arm, a shoulder, a head above the bolster. Every occupied seat visibly holds its person.
6. HANDS AND FEET — whole film: the source shows only WHERE hands and feet are; in the output they are always complete human anatomy — gloved five-fingered hands with natural aged knuckles, a real leg in wool trousers, a real foot in a polished brown leather shoe. THE SHIFT GESTURE at 9.33-10.33s: his right hand travels DOWN from above and lands flat ON TOP of the bakelite knob — palm capping the dome, fingers draping over it — the approach is vertical, from above, the whole way.
7. TEXT-FREE WORLD: every sign is a blank painted shape, every gauge face carries tick marks only, every license plate is a blank plate, the police cars wear plain white roundels.
8. WORLD DRESSING: every roadside vertical is a steel lamppost or a guardrail post; the ground everywhere is asphalt, dirt and dead grass; the source's placeholder blocks appear as the real objects their positions imply — a person's body and clothes, pedals and legs, luggage, crates by the walls.
9. VEHICLE COUNT: shots 1-17 contain exactly one car — the hero car. In SHOT 18 the two POLICE CARS appear ONLY as a reflection inside the wing mirror glass — visible, readable, closing in — while the road ahead holds the hero car alone. In SHOT 19 exactly three vehicles drive on screen: the hero car ahead and the two POLICE CARS behind.

Two-tone: aged sea-teal body, cream roof, softly weathered, gold sunset reflections on the curves. Wheels: painted steel with six ventilation slots, polished chrome hubcaps and trim rings, thin whitewall tires — identical on all four corners in every shot.

Brown tweed jacket over olive cardigan and checked shirt, wool trousers, polished brown shoes, old brown leather driving gloves. Cap, glasses and moustache present in every shot of his face.
THE GRANDMA (front-right) — a composed elegant woman of about seventy: soft round face, rosy cheeks, bright eyes behind round silver spectacles, silver low bun, pearl earrings. STYLE
High-contrast BLACK-AND-WHITE INK ILLUSTRATION brought to motion — a moving manga page. ONE PEN DRAWS EVERYTHING: the people, the car, the streets and the sky are all made of the same rough brush linework with thick-to-thin strokes, deep solid black fills, crisp white negative space and fine film grain — every frame reads as drawn on paper, purely hand-drawn 2D animation, flat as a printed page, never 3D, never photoreal, never live-action.
THE PEOPLE ARE DRAWINGS, the same medium as the world: faces built from confident ink OUTLINES on flat paper-white or flat grey — skin is blank flat paper tone with ZERO texture, shaded ONLY by cross-hatching, screentone dots and solid black shadow shapes; eyes are graphic ink shapes with a white catchlight dot; hair is a mass of drawn ink strokes; hands are line-drawn with inked knuckle creases. Every fold of clothing is a drawn line, every shadow on a face is hatching or a hard black fill — flat 2D drawing conventions on every close-up of every person.
Motion is drawn: smeared ink streaks for speed, snapping poses, rigid stable geometry between poses. Shading sits exactly where the source shades. SELECTIVE COLOR — EXACTLY TWO COLORED OBJECTS IN THE FILM: THE GIRL's rich RED dress and lips, and THE CAR's PINK body — both laid as flat printed ink over the drawing. Everything else, including the police cars and their beacons, is black, white and grey. Lighting is one hard monochrome evening: low blazing sun as hard white key, long solid-black shadows, blown white sky, black-white-black sun strobe through posts in driving shots. Tire smoke is white ink wash.

ACTING — inside the existing shots only. The performance NEVER earns a new shot, a new angle or a closer framing: it is visible only within the 19 listed shots, at exactly the size and distance the source camera gives, and only where the source already shows a face; everywhere else it reads through posture and hands alone.
Shared unspoken game: make this escape look easy — neither will be the first to admit the chase scares them. HE plays for her — every maneuver landed so clean it looks lazy, and where his face is in frame his eyes flick to her for half a beat and snap back to the road. SHE refuses to look rattled — porcelain-calm, hands folded, watching him more than the road, a smile she keeps suppressing; the mirror keeps pulling her eyes. Natural blink cadence, gaze always engaged, never a frozen glassy stare.

NATE — a GROWN MAN, calm and composed on the surface, shy underneath — not a teenager, nothing boyish, nothing comedic. His acting is SIMPLE and QUIET: he keeps himself small and still, spends words carefully, and the shyness reads as RESTRAINT — held-in, a little constrained: a beat of hesitation before each line, lines landing quieter than planned, one micro glance-away, a soft swallow before the question — and then stillness again; SUBTLE, never overplayed, never fidgety. Motive: he has ridden ten floors rehearsing one word. Goal: a name exchange before her floor. His body refuses the easy move — he cannot turn toward her, so everything travels through the lean, the wave, the eyes. THE BREAK: the timid one suddenly humming to her — the laugh escapes before she approves it, and she meets the held look instead of deflecting. In shot 3 she exits SMILING — the warm private smile carried out of frame, the earbud going back in, the day resuming, pleasantly; she never looks back.
